text:
sam: Heads-up — nightly CI just went red on runtime unit tests. Seeing intermittent failures in timer_entropy_test on macos-latest. Link: <https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/1777777777|build 1777777777>
ci-bot: Build failed: tests/runtime/test_timer_entropy.py::test_timer_entropy (1 failed, 42 passed) :exclamation:
sam: small log snippet:```
ASSERT scheduler_clock.cc:142: seed == expected_seed (expected 42, got 278)
stack: runtime::Timer::wake -> runtime::Scheduler::dispatch -> test main
```
jia: ugh, that looks like nondeterministic seed/timer ordering. Has anyone tried re-running with fixed RNG seed or disabling jitter? :thinking:
sam: I tried re-running locally with TASK_SCHED_JITTER=0 and got a green run once, but CI still flakes. Quick repro command I used: `TASK_SCHED_JITTER=0 pytest tests/runtime/test_timer_entropy.py -q -k timer_entropy`
tess: can we queue a CI rerun pinned to the same node image + env? sometimes macos infra differs. @infra-bot can you pin and rerun?
infra-bot: received. pinning to macos-12-small image and preserving build artifacts. rerun queued: <https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/1777777789|run 1777777789>
alex: if disabling jitter makes it stable, maybe the test assumes deterministic wake ordering. We should either make the test resilient (loop until condition with timeout) or add deterministic scheduler harness. Quick triage: can someone run a seed sweep to find common failing seeds?
jia: I'll kick off a seed sweep on a dev machine (small range 0..1023) and report back. If we see clustering, we can add a reproduce-case.
sam: thanks. also, small suggestion: add `--capture=no` to CI run so we can get full stdout next time. Current log truncated the timer trace.
ci-bot: rerun 1777777789 started on macos-12-small. Logs live at <https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/1777777789/logs|logs>
tess: pinging test owners for quick patch: tests/runtime/test_timer_entropy.py @alex @jia — can you review a flaky fix? maybe switch to `await_eventually` pattern rather than exact ordering. :thumbsup:
alex: will take a look in ~1h. If we can't stabilize quickly, we should mark test xfail on macos to keep nightly green and open an issue to fix determinism.
jia: seed sweep started. I'll post summarized findings in this thread.
sam: thanks all — tagging this as triage:repro-needed. If someone gets a minimal repro, post it here and we can bisect across commits/PRs.
ci-bot: update: rerun 1777777789 completed — 1 failure reproduces. Artifact: <https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/1777777789/timer_dump.log|timer_dump.log>
jia: initial sweep found 3 seeds that fail repeatedly: 278, 901, 714. attaching local script to reproduce:```bash
for s in 278 901 714; do 
  TASK_SCHED_SEED=$s TASK_SCHED_JITTER=1 pytest tests/runtime/test_timer_entropy.py::test_timer_entropy -q || echo "seed $s failed";
done
```
sam: perfect. I'll open a bisect job next to narrow code range. @alex can you block time for a quick root-cause pairing later today?
alex: yep, I can join in 2pm PT.
infra-bot: bisect job created: <https://ci.internal/redwood/bisects/1777777799|bisect 1777777799> — it will run across commits in last 200 merges with seeds [278,901,714].
tess: temporary mitigation: I'm going to mark test xfail on macos in the test matrix to keep the nightly green. I'll file a follow-up issue referencing this thread.
sam: sounds good. thanks everyone for the quick responses. keep updates here. :rocket:
